off.label: Off
off.hint: Default. Native haptic feedback only (channels 2 + 3 of the USB audio stream).

fallback.label: Fallback
fallback.hint: Derived haptic fires only when the game has been silent on the native haptic path for ~1 s. Preserves native haptic feedback (Spider-Man Remastered, etc.) while filling in for games that send no haptic data (Ghost of Tsushima on Linux, etc.).

mix.label: Mix
mix.hint: Always add derived haptic on top of native, soft-clipped together. Best for adding more body to games with weak native haptic feedback.

replace.label: Replace
replace.hint: Always use derived; discard native completely. Uniform feel across all games regardless of what they send.

haptics.audioBufferSub: Lower: less audio delay. Higher: steadier audio if it crackles.

games.title: Game setup
games.intro: Checks your launchers for settings that stop adaptive triggers and haptic feedback from reaching games. Checking only reads your settings. Nothing changes until you review the changes and press Apply, and every change can be undone.

why.defaultSteam: Steam currently runs Windows games with {{current}}. Our build is what makes adaptive triggers and haptic feedback work through {{device}}. Games you've set to a specific Proton keep their own setting.
why.defaultHeroic: Heroic currently gives new Epic, GOG and Amazon installs {{current}}. This only affects games you install from now on; installed games keep their own setting, and this page checks those one by one.
why.defaultLutris: Lutris currently uses {{current}} for Wine games. Games with their own Wine version keep it.
why.runner: {{support}} It currently runs with {{current}}, which doesn't pass the controller's native features through.
why.runnerMissing: {{game}} is set to {{current}}, which is no longer installed, so the game can't start.
why.steamInput: {{support}} Steam Input is switched on for this game, so Steam translates the controller into a generic gamepad and the game never sees the DualSense. This is the same as Properties → Controller → "Disable Steam Input" in Steam.
why.envSteam: {{vars}} makes Proton present the controller as an Xbox pad, which turns off adaptive triggers. The launch options become: {{options}}
why.preferSdlWindows: {{vars}} only works with Proton on Linux. On Windows it does nothing, so the option an earlier version added is taken out again. The launch options become: {{options}}
why.envHeroic: {{vars}} makes Proton present the controller as an Xbox pad, which turns off adaptive triggers.
why.audioRule: {{file}} switches the DualSense's audio card to the pro-audio profile, which makes GE-Proton 11 send zero-force triggers and no haptic feedback. The file is renamed to .disabled (not deleted) and the audio service (WirePlumber) restarts, so sound drops for a second.
why.audioProfile: The DualSense's audio card is on "{{profile}}", which makes GE-Proton 11 send zero-force triggers and no haptic feedback. No files change; it's the same as picking the profile in your sound settings.
why.gamepad: {{game}} only works with Xbox-style (XInput) controllers, and our Proton passes the DualSense through as itself, so the game sees no controller. PROTON_PREFER_SDL=1 makes Proton hand it to this game as a standard gamepad, with rumble.{{runner}}
why.gamepadSteam: {{game}} only works with Xbox-style (XInput) controllers, and our Proton passes the DualSense through as itself, so the game sees no controller. PROTON_PREFER_SDL=1 makes Proton hand it to this game as a standard gamepad, with rumble. The launch options become: {{options}}{{runner}}
why.gamepadRunner: {{current}} ignores this option, so the game also switches to {{proton}}.
why.hdrSteam: {{game}} supports HDR. It will run inside gamescope (Valve's compositor), full screen on {{screen}} ({{mode}}), which gives it HDR. Turn on HDR in the game's own settings. If the game misbehaves, Undo puts it back. The launch options become: {{options}}{{runner}}
why.hdrRunner: It also moves to {{proton}}, our DualSense Proton, so the controller's adaptive triggers and haptic feedback work with HDR.
why.hdrHeroic: {{game}} supports HDR. It will run inside gamescope (Valve's compositor), full screen on {{screen}} ({{mode}}), which gives it HDR: Heroic's own Gamescope settings for the game are filled in, and its Enable Wine-Wayland and Enable HDR switches are turned off. Turn on HDR in the game's own settings. If the game misbehaves, Undo puts it back.{{runner}}
why.hdrLutris: {{game}} supports HDR. It will run inside gamescope (Valve's compositor), full screen on {{screen}} ({{mode}}), which gives it HDR: Lutris's own Gamescope options for the game are turned on, HDR included. Turn on HDR in the game's own settings. If the game misbehaves, Undo puts it back.{{runner}}
why.hdrNoProton: Install our DualSense Proton on the Proton card to get the controller's adaptive triggers and haptic feedback with HDR too.
why.hdrOld: {{game}} still has the old HDR setting (PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND / PROTON_ENABLE_HDR), which can leave the game on a black screen. It's removed. {{next}}
why.hdrOldOnly: HDR through gamescope is offered once the checklist on the game's page is all ✓.
why.modeSteam: {{game}} starts in another graphics mode by default and only offers {{feature}} in {{api}}. The game argument {{flag}} starts it in {{api}}; Undo takes it out again. The launch options become: {{args}}{{proton}}
why.modeHeroic: {{game}} starts in another graphics mode by default and only offers {{feature}} in {{api}}. The game argument {{flag}} starts it in {{api}}; Undo takes it out again. Its game arguments in Heroic become: {{args}}{{proton}}
why.modeLutris: {{game}} starts in another graphics mode by default and only offers {{feature}} in {{api}}. The game argument {{flag}} starts it in {{api}}; Undo takes it out again. Its arguments in Lutris become: {{args}}{{proton}}
why.modeVkd3d: Under Proton, DirectX 12 runs through vkd3d-proton, so the first starts can take longer while shaders are built.

tour.helpHint: The quick guided tour from the first start.

welcome.title: Welcome!
welcome.body: Let's take a one-minute tour, with your controller in your hands. Press ✕ to continue and ○ to go back. Esc or Skip tour stops it any time.
welcome.bodyAsk: A one-minute tour, with your controller in your hands. Esc or Skip tour stops it any time.

press.title: This is your controller, live
press.body: Press a few different buttons on your controller and watch them light up here.
press.done: Nice! Everything you press shows up here.

trigger.title: Now the triggers
trigger.body: Now pull a trigger, L2 or R2, all the way down. Feel anything?
trigger.done: Feel that? That's an adaptive trigger: it pushes back, then snaps through. Games use it for guns, bows and brakes.

click.title: Set things up with the mouse
click.body: Click the glowing light bar beside the touch pad with your mouse. Every part of the drawing opens its own settings.
click.done: That opened the light bar settings.

panel.title: Settings open here
panel.body: Changes go to {{device}} right away, so you see, hear and feel them as you go. ✕ closes the panel.

list.title: Or pick from the list
list.body: Not sure where something lives on the controller? Every setting is also here, one click away. » hides this panel for a bigger controller.

save.title: Keep what you like
save.body: Changes are live but temporary. Save to {{device}} keeps them after it powers off; Revert goes back to what's saved.

top.title: {{deviceName}}, your games, and help
top.body: {{deviceName}}: firmware updates, the OLED, power and USB. Games: get Steam and other launchers ready for triggers and haptic feedback (Linux). About: what's new and the guide. ⚙: the app's own settings.

finish.title: You're all set
finish.body: Have fun! You can replay this tour any time from ⚙ App settings.

tour.voiceAsk: Want her to talk you through it? She speaks only through your controller's speaker; you can change it any time in ⚙ App settings.

data.title: Everything, live
data.body: Down here: the sticks, triggers, motion, battery and the link, all as numbers and graphs, as your controller moves.

tour.keepPlaying: Keep playing as long as you like; hold ✕ when you're ready.

typeHint.custom: Your own curve through four points.

curves.customHint: Drag the points, or select one (Tab) and move it with the arrow keys; Shift moves it further.
curves.graph: Sensitivity curve: stick tilt across, output up
curves.gameOn: A game's profile has its own curves on right now. Saving here ends them until that game starts again.
curves.readFailed: {{device, capitalize}} didn't answer with its curves.
curves.saveHint: Saved in {{device}} for the controller in pairing slot {{slot}}; applies to every game right away.
curves.profileHint: Applied only while the game runs. Pick a preset per stick here; your own custom curve is set in Calibration.

ctrlInfo.title: Controller info
ctrlInfo.needsFirmware: Update {{device}}'s firmware to see the controller's firmware, battery voltage and lifetime counters.
ctrlInfo.noController: Connect a controller to see its info.

chargeState.temperatureError: Charging stopped: too hot or too cold

ctrlInfo.tooOld: This controller's firmware is too old for lifetime counters (update it on a PS5 or with Sony's PlayStation Accessories app).
ctrlInfo.noCounters: This controller didn't send lifetime counters.
ctrlInfo.privacy: Kept by the controller itself. Read only: nothing is changed, and its serial number is never read into the app.
ctrlInfo.howToPc: Plug the controller into a Windows PC with a USB-C cable and update it with Sony's PlayStation Accessories app (formerly "Firmware updater for DualSense wireless controller").
ctrlInfo.howToPs5: Or on a PS5: connect it with a USB cable, then Settings → Accessories → Controller (General) → DualSense Wireless Controller Device Software.
ctrlInfo.howToCable: The update can't go through {{device}}. Afterwards, pair the controller with {{device}} again if it doesn't reconnect.
ctrlInfo.windowsOnly: Sony's PlayStation Accessories app runs on Windows only: on Linux and macOS, use a Windows PC or a PS5.

stickTest.circleHow: Roll each stick slowly around its edge a few times. The outline shows how far it reaches in every direction.
stickTest.notYet: Not rolled around the edge yet
stickTest.overUnder: Past the circle in {{over}} of them, short of it in {{under}}
stickTest.short: Doesn't reach the edge: push it all the way.
stickTest.circleGood: Average error is how far the outline is from the circle. Under about 10% is typical for a healthy DualSense.
stickTest.driftHow: Leave the sticks alone for {{seconds}} seconds: this records where they rest and whether they move.
stickTest.driftStats: Max {{max}} · average {{avg}} from the center (of full tilt)
stickTest.driftWarn: Possible stick drift: it moves noticeably at rest. Calibration above can center it, or raise the deadzone.
stickTest.driftHidden: Moves a little at rest, but the deadzone hides it from games.

timing.title: Timing
timing.hint: How long each part of the firmware takes: the average and the worst case since the reset. The worst case shows jitter; the core1 speaker frame must stay well under 10 ms per frame, or audio drops.
timing.usTimer: Measured with the microsecond timer (the CPU's cycle counter isn't available), so short stages are rounded.

specs.title: Specs
specs.notDetected: Not detected: {{device}} drives it whenever it's attached.

hdr.label: HDR lighting (experimental)
hdr.sub: The light bar glows brighter than white on an HDR display, like the real LEDs. Needs hardware acceleration; applies at restart.

grips.testHint: Vibrates that side for 3 s at its vibration intensity now; press it again to stop early (the trigger tests don't use these: L2 and R2 have their own motors).

channel.label: Update channel
channel.devHint: Development builds of the app and the firmware, before they're released: newer, and less tested. You also get every stable release. Back to stable installs the latest stable app and firmware.
channel.joinNewer: You get builds of the app and of {{device}}'s firmware before they're released: newer features, sooner.
channel.joinBoth: Both are offered: the app updates itself, the firmware update shows under {{deviceName}} as usual.
channel.joinBugs: They're less tested than stable releases and can have bugs. Please report what you find.
channel.joinBack: Back to stable (App settings → Updates) returns to the latest stable app and firmware at any time.
channel.joinNoNotes: No notes for this build in the feed yet.
channel.joinNotesLink: Read the release notes on GitHub
channel.joinOffline: Can't reach the development feed right now (offline?). You can still join; the update shows when it's reachable.

layouts.title: Button layouts
layouts.hint: Save the buttons above under a name. A game's profile can use a layout: it's switched in while the game runs (never saved on {{device}}), and your normal buttons come back when it ends.
layouts.loadHint: Put this layout into the editor above (Apply assignments makes it your normal buttons)
layouts.deleteHint: Delete this layout (games using it go back to your normal buttons)
layouts.activeNotice: {{game}}'s button layout is on {{device}} now. Apply assignments saves your normal buttons and ends it until the game starts again.
layouts.needsFirmware: Needs the newest firmware on {{device}} ({{deviceName}} → Update).
layouts.noneForGame: Save layouts on the Buttons page: pick a button on the controller.
layouts.allHint_one: {{count}} button changed from the controller's own. Pick from this list or click a button on the drawing; both change the same thing.
layouts.allHint_other: {{count}} buttons changed from the controller's own. Pick from this list or click a button on the drawing; both change the same thing.
layouts.shortcutSub: Every button in one list, saved layouts for games
layouts.seeAll: See all buttons and saved layouts

loadedState.notApplied: Not applied yet: Apply assignments makes it your normal buttons on {{device}}.
loadedState.edited: Changed since you loaded it: Update saves the changes into the layout; Apply assignments makes them your normal buttons.
loadedState.applied: Applied: these are your normal buttons on {{device}} now.

editing.title: Editing: {{title}} profile
editing.hint: settings changed here are felt right away, buttons and curves once saved; Save to profile keeps them all for this game. Your normal settings come back with Done.
editing.unsaved: You have unsaved changes to {{title}}'s profile.
editing.openHint: Put this profile on the controller and edit it with every panel, feeling each change live
editing.buttonsNote: {{title}}'s profile is on: buttons go into this game's layout with Save to profile, not into your normal buttons.
editing.dongleNote: Not part of {{title}}'s profile: these settings on {{device}} stay your normal ones. Changes here are kept after the profile ends; save them to {{device}} then.
editing.calibrationNote: Calibration belongs to the controller, not to {{title}}'s profile: saving it changes it in {{device}} for every game.
editing.curvesNote: {{title}}'s profile is on: curves go into this game's profile with Save to profile and are felt from then on; your normal curves come back after.
editing.curvesNormal: This stick uses your normal curve in this game.

profile.changes: What this game changes (everything else uses your normal settings):
profile.allNormal: Nothing changed for this game yet: it uses your normal settings. Edit in controller view to change any of them for this game.
profile.copyHint: This game gets the settings on {{device}} now
profile.applyFailed: {{title}}'s profile didn't go on {{device}} ({{reason}}). Your normal settings are on.
profile.partlyOn: {{title}}'s profile may be on without its buttons or stick curves ({{reason}}). It's tried again when {{device}} reconnects.
profile.notOn: {{title}}'s profile isn't on {{device}} yet, so nothing was saved into it. Try again once it's on.

wayland.no: Wayland session: this desktop runs on X11. Log out and pick the Wayland session (Plasma or GNOME) on the login screen.

off.kde: No screen has HDR on: turn it on in System Settings → Display & Monitor (High Dynamic Range).
off.gnome: No screen has HDR on: turn it on in Settings → Displays (HDR, GNOME 48 or later).

screen.other-desktop: The app can read the HDR setting only on KDE Plasma 6 and GNOME 48 or later, so Turn on HDR isn't offered on this desktop. You can still set it up yourself.
screen.failed: The app couldn't read the screen settings (kscreen-doctor or GNOME's display settings), so Turn on HDR isn't offered.

gamescope.no: gamescope isn't installed: install your distribution's gamescope package, version {{min}} or later (the Guide says how).
gamescope.unknown: gamescope is installed but didn't say its version: HDR needs {{min}} or later.
gamescope.old: gamescope {{version}} is too old: HDR needs {{min}} or later. Update it from your distribution.
gamescope.flatpakNo: Your launcher is a Flatpak: install gamescope for it with flatpak install flathub {{ext}} (the branch that matches the launcher's runtime).

layer.ok: gamescope's HDR layer (WSI Vulkan layer) installed
layer.no: gamescope's HDR layer (VkLayer_FROG_gamescope_wsi) is missing: it comes with gamescope on most distributions; reinstall gamescope, or install the package that has it.

proton.no: Our DualSense Proton isn't installed: install it on the Proton card for the controller's adaptive triggers and haptic feedback with HDR.

runner.ok: The game runs on our DualSense Proton
runner.no: The game runs on {{runner}}: Turn on HDR also moves it to our DualSense Proton (adaptive triggers and haptic feedback with HDR).

setup.set: Set up: the game runs inside gamescope with HDR
setup.needed: Not set up yet: Turn on HDR above does it
setup.update: It still has the old HDR setting (black screen): the change above replaces it
setup.missing: Not set up: Turn on HDR is offered once everything above is ✓

hdrManual.title: Set it up yourself
hdrManual.intro: What Turn on HDR does, by hand. Other Proton builds may work with gamescope too; our DualSense Proton is the one we test (HDR plus the controller's adaptive triggers and haptic feedback).
hdrManual.noMode: No screen was read, so this uses 3840×2160: put your screen's resolution after -W and -H.
hdrManual.noProton: our DualSense Proton (install it on the Proton card)

steam.proton: In Steam, the game's Properties → Compatibility: tick Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool and pick {{proton}}.
steam.line: Properties → General → Launch Options: paste this line (made for {{screen}} at {{mode}}; keep anything you already had there):

heroic.proton: In Heroic, the game's Settings → Wine Version: pick {{proton}}.
heroic.gamescope: Settings → Gamescope: turn on Enables Upscaling; Game Width and Upscale Width {{width}}, Game Height and Upscale Height {{height}}; window type Fullscreen; Additional Options:
heroic.env: Settings → Advanced → Environment Variables: add {{env}}. In Settings → Other, turn off Enable Wine-Wayland and Enable HDR if they're on.

lutris.proton: In Lutris, the game's Configure → Runner options → Wine version: pick {{proton}}.
lutris.gamescope: Configure → System options (tick Advanced) → Gamescope: turn on Enable Gamescope, Enable HDR and Relative Mouse Mode; Output Resolution and Game Resolution {{width}}x{{height}}; Window Mode Fullscreen; Custom Settings:
lutris.env: System options → Environment variables: add {{env}}, and remove PROTON_ENABLE_WAYLAND and PROTON_ENABLE_HDR if they're there.

hdrManual.inGame: Start the game and turn on HDR in its own display settings.
hdrManual.guide: The Guide (About page) explains each part: Games → HDR in games on Linux.
